newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Falklanders warm to Argentina - Foreign Minister.
newsitem.headline: Falklanders warm to Argentina - Foreign Minister.

text.p: Argentine Foreign Minister Guido Di Tella said on Wednesday the attitude of residents of the disputed Falkland Islands towards Argentina had vastly improved because of his "charm offensive".
"I have no doubt whatsoever that the 'charm policy' has been a success," Di Tella told local radio.
"If you read the (Falklands newspaper) Penguin News, which reflects the islanders' opinion towards Argentina, it has changed in a radical way."
He said the islanders used to have a "completely hostile" attitude towards Argentina but "Their discomfort with us has changed. And that is all there is to our 'charm policy.'"

Argentina and Britain fought a brief but bloody war in 1982 in which about 1,000 soldiers, mostly Argentine, died. Argentina lost the war but maintains its claim to sovereignty over the South Atlantic islands that it calls the Malvinas.

Di Tella's "charm offensive" has included sending the islanders Christmas cards with photos of his family, books and video cassettes. Recently, his gestures have attracted criticism in Argentina, with opposition politicians claiming they had not managed to win the country any concessions.
Di Tella contended it would be "childish" to think a bunch of letters and small gifts would change a 150-year-old policy. "That is not the centre of our foreign policy," he said.
"Our strategy has been to make Argentina into a serious and responsible country. And today Argentina is listened to in a way that was not possible 10 years ago."
Diplomatic ties with Britain resumed soon after President Carlos Menem took office in 1989.
